$comment: Layer 13 WP-13.2 (write/edit + the shared mutation queue) canonical shape, discriminated by a top-level `builtin_mutation` key. Scenarios live in conformance/agent/builtin-mutation/ (their own directory, so the WP-13.1 `builtin_tool` runners are unaffected). A runner builds `fixture` (plus a case's own `fixture`) under a FRESH temporary root for every case or queue scenario, wraps the real local ctx.fs in each declared provider (scripted answers and gates for named paths, every call recorded), constructs the REAL write/edit tools over those providers, and runs every call through the REAL Layer 06 execute pipeline (prepare_arguments, schema validation, execute). The runner performs no tool logic. PATHS: a path a tool passes to ctx.fs is recorded verbatim when relative, and relative to the fixture root ('/'-separated, '.' for the root) when absolute; scripted answers and gates match that same recorded form. Unscripted, ungated calls go to the real provider unchanged.

witnesses.$comment: The pi-parity-manifest `tests:` names this scenario closes.

provider.$comment: scripting shared by every provider of the scenario

symlink.$comment: link target, relative to the fixture root

text.$comment: written as UTF-8, byte for byte (no newline translation)

without_exec_009.$comment: check_read_write returns not_supported for every path (a provider lacking EXEC-009, spec/execution.md section 13.5 FALLBACK)

without_exec_008.$comment: check_readable returns not_supported for every path (a provider lacking EXEC-008)

fileAfter.$comment: the fixture file's state after the case/scenario: its exact bytes, or absent

fixture.$comment: added to the scenario fixture for this case only

signal.$comment: the call's signal is already aborted when the runner invokes the Layer 06 pipeline: Layer 06 preflight answers 'Operation aborted' and never invokes execute, so no ctx.fs call is made (L13-WP132-R004). The tool's own register-before-check rule is witnessed with abort_after / a queue abort step instead

abort_after.$comment: the runner aborts the call's signal as the FIRST invocation of the named ctx.fs operation hands back its (real or scripted) answer -- before the tool resumes

arguments.$comment: the raw tool-call arguments, before prepare_arguments. Object-valued: Layer 02/05 ToolCall arguments are a JSON object, so prepareEditArguments' non-object branch is prepare-helper authority evidence only, not an integration case (L13-WP132-R005)

unpaired_surrogate_arguments.$comment: the arguments contain an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate. Whether a binding can receive such an argument is decided at Layer 02/05 (spec/tools.md WP-13.2, String semantics: recorded, not resolved). A binding whose argument decoding carries it MUST pass the case; one whose decoding cannot represent it MUST show the argument is rejected before the tool runs, and records that as the Layer 02/05 hazard, not as a pass

argument_validation_failure.$comment: the prepared arguments fail the tool's parameter schema: Layer 06's certified immediate argument-validation error (its text is Layer 06's, not asserted here); execute never runs and no ctx.fs call is made

details.$comment: the tool's own details, exact; {} means none

fs_calls.$comment: every ctx.fs call in order, as '<operation> <recorded path>'

queue.$comment: Concurrent calls. The runner creates one wrapped ctx.fs per `providers` id (default one provider, `p`) over the SAME fixture root -- distinct provider instances, so distinct queue scopes -- and one write and one edit tool per provider. It starts every call in list order WITHOUT awaiting any (each call is begun before the next is started), then quiesces; then applies each step in order, quiescing after each; then requires every call to have settled (a call still pending with no gate held is a failure: a lingering queue entry or a lost wake-up). QUIESCE: run the binding's scheduler until no task can make progress without a gate being released. A task waiting on a timer CAN make progress: every timer due within a generous horizon must be fired (e.g. by advancing a virtual clock) before the next step -- a fixed real-time settle window is not quiescence, since a longer timer outlives it (L13-WP132-I001). The log records, per provider, every ctx.fs invocation's start and its answer, and every call's result.

gates.$comment: each named invocation (the `occurrence`-th invocation of `operation` on `path` through `provider`, 1-based) blocks before reaching the real provider until a step releases it

release.$comment: a gate id: the held invocation proceeds to the real provider

error.$comment: with release: the held invocation answers this error instead of reaching the provider

abort.$comment: abort that call's signal. Every call starts with a live signal and passes Layer 06 preflight; an abort step therefore reaches the tool's own checkpoints (L13-WP132-R004)

results.$comment: per call id: is_error, exact text and (optionally) exact details

order.$comment: each pair [a, b]: event a is logged, and before event b if b is logged at all (use `logged` to require b). EVENT NAMES: '<provider> <operation> <recorded path> #<n> start' and '<provider> <operation> <recorded path> #<n> ok|<error code>' (n = that provider's 1-based invocation count for that operation and path), and 'result <call id>'
